subject: Azure Marketplace: offer region mapping, networking evidence, and license allocation
messages:
From: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@acme-analytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Azure Marketplace: offer region mapping, networking evidence, and license allocation

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the onboarding call this morning. We started mapping our SaaS offer for Azure and ran into a few things the portal wasn't explicit about. Can you confirm the following so we can finish the publisher account setup and submit the initial offer?

- Region mapping: We plan to list a global SaaS offer but want to restrict data residency for EU customers to the West Europe region. Does the Marketplace require separate SKUs per region for residency, or is metadata sufficient?
- Networking evidence: The portal asks for "networking architecture proof" — will a short network diagram plus a Private Link configuration snippet be enough, or do they require packet-level logs / test curl outputs?
- Licensing allocation: Our license server returns entitlements from our central tenant. For co-sell and marketplace SKU reporting, do we need to provide a per-SKU license allocation spreadsheet (we can generate one) or is a single entitlement endpoint sufficient?

I've attached a draft network diagram and a preliminary license mapping file for your review (networking-evidence.pdf, license-mapping.xlsx).

If you prefer, we can route questions to the Azure MPX support alias, but want to surface anything Redwood-specific first so we submit a clean package.

Thanks,
Aisha Gupta
Director, Cloud Partnerships
Acme Analytics

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace: offer region mapping, networking evidence, and license allocation

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for sending these over — the attachments look like a good start. Quick answers below, then a short checklist you can use before submission: 

- Region mapping: For a global SaaS offer with residency guarantees you should create separate SKUs (or separate offers) if you need strict data residency claims. Metadata alone is often rejected during certification if it implies per-region data segregation without a SKU-level signal. Different SKUs also make co-sell reporting clearer.

- Networking evidence: The portal usually accepts a network diagram plus Private Link configuration details and an outbound IP allowlist. You do not need packet captures; however, provide a curl-based connectivity check (example in my checklist) and a short note on how the KV/cache and session affinity are handled across regions.

- Licensing allocation: Provide a per-SKU allocation workbook — Azure's co-sell/measures team expects SKU-level mapping for usage reporting. The entitlement endpoint can be included as evidence but won't replace the SKU spreadsheet during initial validation.

Checklist before submission to Azure MPX:
1) SKU mapping CSV (SKU id, name, region, plan, price model) — see attached sku-mapping.csv
2) License mapping workbook per SKU (included)
3) Networking diagram (annotated) + Private Link config snippet
4) Simple connectivity check script (curl) and expected responses
5) Legal entity & DUNS + commercial contact and marketplace contact
6) DocuSign link for the publisher agreement (if not already signed)

I'll loop Marissa for the co-sell readiness / marketing assets, and Karthik on the identity/provisioning pieces. If you'd like, I can open a ticket with mpx-support and include our recommended evidence pack to speed the cert gate.

-Connor
Principal Partner Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace: offer region mapping, networking evidence, and license allocation

Hi Aisha / team,

Adding a couple of operational notes from the publisher enablement side: 

- Co-sell eligibility: To be co-sell ready you'll want the offer to include a defined commercial contact and co-sell lead (email + phone). We also check that the offer listing includes a clear customer success playbook (2–3 bullets) so sellers can hit DISCOVERY quickly.
- Offer metadata: Include a short "data residency" sentence in the offer description and ensure the SKU long name includes the region tag (e.g., "Pro — West Europe").
- Marketplace portal tips: When uploading the SKU mapping, use the CSV format the portal accepts (we've found commas in SKU descriptions sometimes corrupt the fields). I can export a template if useful.

Karthik — can you confirm if we need SPN delegation for the provisioning hooks or if the portal service principal is sufficient for the initial certification run?

Aisha — once Connor confirms the final files feel free to drop everything into the shared onboarding Drive folder and I'll stage the portal submission. If you want me to attach marketing collateral for co-sell enablement now (one-pager + demo recording), let me know.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace: offer region mapping, networking evidence, and license allocation

Thanks both — this is super helpful. We'll: 
- Generate separate SKUs for "Global" and "West Europe (data residency)"
- Update the license mapping to include SKU IDs and price plans and reupload the CSV
- Add the curl connectivity checks and a short note on session affinity in the networking PDF

Karthik - please confirm SPN delegation requirement; if it's required we'll coordinate with our infra lead to get credentials in place.

I'll place the revised artifacts in the shared Drive link and ping you when it's ready for you to stage the portal submission. If we hit any odd validation errors from MPX we'll route those back to Connor for support.

Appreciate the quick turnaround—aiming to submit by end of week.

Regards,
Aisha Gupta
Director, Cloud Partnerships
Acme Analytics
